goal: Initialize existing or empty repositories while preserving user-owned conventions.
invariants: Missing commands are actionable configuration requirements.
Unconfigured architecture setup is schema-valid and never qualifies as a constraint.
The generated and shared runners retain owned command groups through bounded timeout, output-limit and cancellation cleanup even if the leader closes first.
Unsupported CLI action flags fail before repository mutation or execution; only init accepts dry-run.
Missing scoped evidence protection is generated despite root negations; existing ignore bytes are preserved and unsafe conventions are actionable.
Verification targets must be explicitly owned configuration entries; absent inherited names cannot satisfy maps, readiness or command execution, while valid own names retain literal argv.

Guided adoption planning is deterministic and read-only; supplied facts and discovered candidates remain distinct, and separate application preserves unrelated bytes, requires current snapshots and pre-change authorization, and retains originals for reviewable recovery.
acceptance: One capability can be proposed and configured through reviewed exact-byte operations without executing application commands or claiming behavioral evidence.
CLI init and dry-run report actionable missing commands while preserving existing instruction, configuration and policy bytes across repeated invocations.
Initializing empty architecture creates valid incomplete setup; doctor and audit cannot award enforced constraints until real modules and a forbidden edge are configured.
The configured runner preserves literal argument values and underlying exit status, and reports unavailable commands, bounded timeout and output-limit failures.
